title: ADR 0001: Claude Code is the harness, Orca is an optional host
shortDescription: Ang targets Claude Code only; Orca support switches on only when configured and detected

title: ADR 0002: Zero-dependency library script
shortDescription: What ships under src/ uses only Node built-ins, so the library script has no packages and installing Ang needs only Node 26+, npx and git; dev-only tooling outside src/ may carry its own private dependencies

title: ADR 0003: Per-user config is a gitignored overlay limited to LOCAL_KEYS
shortDescription: Root ang.json is committed and project-owned; gitignored ang.local.json may set only host and pilot, and any other key is dropped with a warning

title: ADR 0004: Pilot identity is hook-injected, never templated
shortDescription: The pilot's name reaches agents through the optional pilot feature's rule(value) at session and subagent start; shipped files never contain a name

title: ADR 0005: Install by copy-in from published releases
shortDescription: Ang installs with a stamped install.sh release asset that copies src/ in with pinned giget, only ever onto a published release, with no plugin and no uninstall command

title: ADR 0006: Upgrade by three-way merge
shortDescription: upgrade-ang merges each file three-way against the recorded release, picks one of four routes by conflict count, never commits and is all or nothing; one settings merge serves install and upgrade

title: ADR 0007: How releases are cut
shortDescription: Zac cuts each release with the repo-only /cut-release skill, CI does the mechanics on tag push, notes and upgrade guides are separate files, and every release is rehearsed on a fixture repo

title: ADR 0008: Docs are a Starlight site on GitHub Pages
shortDescription: The user docs are a Starlight site in root docs/, built and published to zacbraddy.github.io/ang/ by one Actions workflow, with relative page links so a custom domain stays a config change

title: ADR 0009: Docs describe the shipped files
shortDescription: The README and docs site describe what the files under src/ actually do; where memory and the files differ the files win, and docs defects become recorded work rather than changes to Ang

title: ADR 0010: Docs publish llms.txt
shortDescription: The docs site publishes llms.txt, llms-full.txt and llms-small.txt for agents through starlight-llms-txt with default settings

title: C4 level 1, context
shortDescription: Who uses Ang and which outside systems it touches; Ang is a set of files inside one repo, run by Claude Code

title: C4 level 2, containers
shortDescription: Ang's containers split into committed, team-wide ones and gitignored, per-user ones, and how Claude Code and the script use each

title: Project structure
shortDescription: What ships (src/), how this repo runs Ang on itself through symlinks, the repo-only release tooling, and where everything else lives
